segments.text: This level is a login form backed by a database, and the source shows the username is concatenated straight into the query, but the page never tells us the password, it only tells us whether a user exists.
I fetch the source and pull out the query, which takes the username straight from the request.

I first confirm the injection works by appending a condition to the username: a double quote, then and password like percent, and the page replies that the user exists, which proves I can test predicates about the password.
I open vim and write a script. The first chunk sets up the request helper: it posts a username to the page and returns true when the reply says the user exists.

The second chunk adds the loop: for each of the thirty-two character positions, it binary searches the character code, asking the database whether the code at that position is greater than a midpoint, and the exists or does not exist reply gives a single bit.
The third chunk finishes the loop: it stops when a position has no character, appends each recovered character, and prints the growing password as it goes.
I run the script, and it prints the password one character at a time, finishing with the full thirty-two characters.
